scenario_source.notes: NHTSA Pre-Crash Scenario 7 — following vehicle strikes lead that is stopped. Baseline strict-RSS parity.

description: 30 m/s into a stopped lead under strict RSS. Hand-computed: 30·1 + 0.5·3·1² + (30+3)²/(2·4) - 0 = 30 + 1.5 + 136.125 = 167.625 m.

scenario_source.notes: Same NHTSA S7 geometry with sensor_fuzz=0.6 on the forward channel (heavy rain / light fog). Demonstrates MGAI superiority: safe distance widens automatically.
NHTSA Pre-Crash Scenario 11 — following vehicle strikes lead that is accelerating / moving faster. Lead moving faster reduces required separation.

description: Ego 25 m/s, lead 35 m/s under strict RSS. Hand-computed: 25 + 1.5 + 784/8 - 1225/16 = 25 + 1.5 + 98 - 76.5625 = 47.9375 m.

scenario_source.notes: NHTSA Pre-Crash Scenario 19 — pedestrian crosses from behind occlusion (parked vehicle). Rule 4 visibility test.

description: 30m of visibility, worst-case walking pedestrian at 2 m/s, urban params (ρ=0.8, a_min_brake=5). v = √(2·5·(30 - 2·0.8)) = √284 ≈ 16.85 m/s (~37 mph cap on urban approach).

scenario_source.notes: NHTSA Pre-Crash Scenario 31 — rear-end conflict, both vehicles moving, lead decelerates. Baseline required safe distance at matched speed.

description: Both at 25 m/s (~56 mph) under strict RSS. Hand-computed: 25 + 1.5 + 784/8 - 625/16 = 25 + 1.5 + 98 - 39.0625 = 85.4375 m.
